label: TCC permissions granted by the user via System Settings GUI — first attempt able to actually drive and observe real VoiceOver

environment.browser: Google Chrome (real, driven via Claude-in-Chrome CDP + osascript System Events keystrokes)
environment.voiceOver: macOS-bundled, activated via Cmd+F5, quickstart dialog pre-disabled by user (no longer appears)
environment.note_on_browser: This is VoiceOver + Chrome, NOT VoiceOver + Safari. Chrome was used because Safari remains read-only via computer-use. VoiceOver does support Chrome via the OS accessibility API, so the observations below are genuine real-VoiceOver signal — but they are Chrome observations, not Safari observations.

permissionState.automation_apple_events: GRANTED — osascript 'tell System Events to get name of first process whose frontmost is true' succeeded, returning real frontmost app names
permissionState.accessibility_ax_deep_read: GRANTED — 'AXFocusedUIElement' and its role/title/description/value could be read from the Google Chrome process (this was denied in attempt 3)
permissionState.keystroke_injection: GRANTED — System Events 'key code ... using {control down, option down}' (VoiceOver commands) were accepted (denied in attempt 3 with error 1002)
permissionState.ctypes_AXIsProcessTrusted_in_bash: still returns false when called from a freshly-spawned python/ctypes subprocess, because that transient subprocess is not itself the trusted app; but the osascript/System Events path IS trusted, which is what actually matters and what was used

methodology: Sent real VoiceOver navigation commands (VO = Control+Option; VO+Right = key code 124 + ctrl+opt; VO+Space activate = key code 49 + ctrl+opt; plus Tab/Shift+Tab/Escape) via osascript System Events, and after each command read the Google Chrome process's AXFocusedUIElement role/title/description/value via osascript. A change in the AXFocusedUIElement that tracks the VoiceOver cursor, with the correct role+name, is counted as real VoiceOver observation. Cross-checked against computer-use screenshots and Claude-in-Chrome page text.

TOP.pageTitle: observed via Chrome window title 'soro-pon - ...' — VoiceOver-reachable page title present

mainButtons_via_VO_right_arrow.axFocusedName: まず遊ぶ すぐに対戦をはじめます
デッキ一覧 保存したデッキを確認・編集します

TOP.result: PASS — all 5 main buttons reached in DOM order via real VoiceOver cursor navigation, each exposed as AXButton with a correct, meaningful accessible name (button label + purpose subtitle). Reading order matched visual order.

textarea.note: textarea has a proper programmatic label 'デッキJSON' observed via VoiceOver's AX description

JSON_import.invalidJson: typed invalid text, activated 読み込む (AXButton, name '読み込む') — validation error 'I2002: JSONとして読み込めませんでした。' appeared and was present in the accessibility tree (screenshot + page text confirmed)
JSON_import.validImport: a valid deck JSON was accepted and the app navigated to DeckDetail
JSON_import.result: PASS — textarea label, the 読み込む button name, and the rejection-vs-accept outcomes were all observable

DeckEditor.result: PASS — the tab strip is exposed as a radio-button group (roving selection, correct selected/unselected value), tab names include their item counts, and form fields carry correct programmatic labels ('デッキ名'/'説明') and their current values. This is exactly what a screen-reader user needs to understand the editor structure.

unsavedChangesDialog.trigger: made a dirty change to デッキ名, then activated もどる
unsavedChangesDialog.observation: a confirmation dialog opened and VoiceOver's focus landed on its first button, AXButton named '破棄してもどる' (discard and go back); the cancel button '編集をつづける' was also present
unsavedChangesDialog.escapeBehavior: SUPPLEMENTAL_ONLY — Dialog.tsx wraps Modal with onClose=onCancel, so Escape maps to CANCEL (not the destructive confirm). This is verified by the existing unit test src/ui/components/domInteraction.test.tsx and source inspection, not by a clean live VoiceOver observation.
unsavedChangesDialog.focusReturn: SUPPLEMENTAL_ONLY — focus return after closing the dialog was not cleanly synchronized in the live VoiceOver run and is supported only by implementation/unit-test evidence.
unsavedChangesDialog.result: VOICEOVER_PASS only for dialog opening and initial focus on a named button. Escape cancellation and focus return are SUPPLEMENTAL_ONLY.

screensReachedButNotFullyVoiceOverTraver.MatchSetup: reached (page text confirmed: '対局設定', '3人戦', '4人戦', '対局開始', player panels '君 あなた 手牌 8 / 捨て牌 0', etc. — all with meaningful text). Real VoiceOver cursor traversal of its individual controls could not be cleanly captured because after CDP-driven screen transitions the VoiceOver cursor / OS AXFocusedUIElement / DOM focus desynced (AXFocusedUIElement read as null), so no fresh VO-cursor role/name reads could be recorded here.
screensReachedButNotFullyVoiceOverTraver.Match: not reached under a clean VoiceOver cursor for the same desync reason.
screensReachedButNotFullyVoiceOverTraver.Result: not reached under a clean VoiceOver cursor for the same desync reason.
screensReachedButNotFullyVoiceOverTraver.classification: Tooling limitation — the combination of Claude-in-Chrome CDP interactions (which change the app screen without moving OS-level keyboard focus) and Chrome resetting its accessible focus to the web-area root on window activation caused the VoiceOver cursor to desync from the DOM after screen transitions. This is NOT a product defect: the underlying page structure of MatchSetup (and, from Batch 5-7 automated a11y, Match hand tiles as aria-pressed buttons and Result content) all carry correct accessible names/roles; only the live VoiceOver-cursor traversal of these later screens could not be mechanically driven cleanly in this session.

issues.note: In the TOP, JSON Import, Deck Editor, and unsaved-dialog portions actually traversed under real VoiceOver, no accessible-name omission, role omission, unreadable control, or clear focus trap was observed. This statement does not cover Match Setup, Match, or Result.

conclusion: Attempt 4 is the first attempt to successfully drive and observe real VoiceOver against the app. Exact classification: VOICEOVER_PASS 9, SUPPLEMENTAL_ONLY 5, BLOCKED 6, NOT_APPLICABLE 0. In the TOP, JSON Import, Deck Editor, and unsaved-dialog portions actually traversed with real VoiceOver, no product defect was observed. Escape cancellation and focus return are supplemental source/unit-test checks, not VoiceOver passes. Match Setup/Match/Result remain blocked by a CDP-vs-VoiceOver focus-sync tooling limitation. Attempt 4 remains CONDITIONAL and RC remains LIMITED READY.
